feedback.answered: The delay-ordering helper's semantics are now understood and its one dangerous premise is bounded. When a latency table is configured, client proposals are passed through a per-connection ordering structure that hands proposals to the replica's propose channel only in a contiguous run starting from CommandId zero (the traversal compares the last handled id with the next node's id minus one, starting from -1). A connection whose first proposal carries any other CommandId would therefore never be delivered: the proposal sits in the structure and the client waits. The premise does not arise in this snapshot: the client numbers its proposals from zero (seqnum initialised to -1 and incremented before use) and creates one connection per run, and although Reconnect exists in the client it has no call site anywhere in the repository, so no connection is ever reused with a continuing command-id sequence.
remaining: the helper's behaviour if a future caller reconnects with a continuing command-id sequence, which would stall that client's proposals
